strengths: Novel and well-articulated problem identification: The 'sink trap' phenomenon reveals a fundamental disconnect between a model's geometric expressivity and linguistic sensitivity that has not been previously studied
Elegant and well-justified technical solution: Using unconditional priors to stabilize inversion trajectories is simple, effective, and doesn't require auxiliary models or image-based priors
Comprehensive experimental validation: Strong quantitative metrics (diversity ratio, L1, LPIPS, SigLIP), multi-dataset evaluation, multiple baselines, and multiview consistency checks
Clear presentation and reproducibility: Well-structured paper with effective visualizations, detailed algorithms in appendices, and use of public models (TRELLIS)
Practical impact: Enables high-fidelity text-based 3D shape editing while maintaining global structure and pose consistency, addressing a real limitation of current systems
Insightful theoretical analysis: Section 4's decomposition of language diversity and geometric expressivity provides valuable understanding of text-to-3D model limitations
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: The core contribution primarily adapts existing null-text inversion techniques from image generation to 3D, with moderate algorithmic innovation
Model-specific approach: Entire framework tightly coupled to TRELLIS; generalization to other 3D generative models is unclear and deferred to future work, limiting broader impact

Narrow evaluation scope: Limited to humanoid/character models (200-280 shapes); no evaluation on diverse object categories (furniture, tools, etc.), raising concerns about generalization beyond characters
Incomplete failure mode resolution: Section 6 acknowledges that extreme OOD cases produce implausible geometries when applying edit prompts, but these failure cases are not addressed or solved
Missing quantitative rigor: Lacks statistical significance testing, error bars/confidence intervals in tables, computational cost analysis, and ablation studies on key hyperparameters
No automatic OOD detection: Requires manual user judgment to apply empty prompts versus text prompts; lacks algorithmic means to automatically detect out-of-distribution conditions
Absent user studies: No human evaluation of editing quality or perceptual naturalness despite claiming practical editing applications

Incomplete theoretical justification: While sink trap is well-characterized empirically, deeper theoretical explanation of why unconditional guidance specifically enables OOD reconstruction is missing
Limited baseline comparisons: VoxHammer fails in 67% of test cases making comparison incomplete; limited comparison with recent 3D-to-3D editing methods and other text-to-3D systems
Hyperparameter complexity: Algorithm 1 involves multiple optimization loops with several hyperparameters; limited sensitivity analysis or ablation studies provided

strengths: Identifies an interesting and concrete failure mode (sink trap phenomenon) in text-to-3D generative models with clear visual illustration
Proposes a simple and practical solution leveraging unconditional priors without requiring auxiliary models
Generally well-written with effective visualizations and transparent discussion of limitations
Provides both quantitative metrics (L1, LPIPS, SigLIP) and qualitative evaluation
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily applies existing techniques (Euler inversion, null-text optimization) to 3D shapes; unclear distinction from prior null-text inversion work

Incomplete analysis of core phenomenon: the explanation for sink trap lacks theoretical rigor; diversity analysis (Section 4.1) is suggestive but insufficient to explain why sparse regions cause insensitivity to prompts

Severely limited experimental scope: evaluated on only TRELLIS (no other 3D generative models), only 80 DT4D shapes, and only simple humanoid/animal characters—insufficient to support generalizability claims
Weak baseline comparisons: VoxHammer comparison appears selective, and missing comparisons with other recent 3D editing methods

Fundamental contradictions undermine core claims: Section 6 acknowledges editing trajectories become unstable and produce implausible geometries, directly contradicting claims about robustness to OOD shapes
Poor editing quality in practice: many results show primarily texture rather than geometric changes; Figures 7 and 9 demonstrate clear failure cases
Narrow applicability: requires access to unconditional generative model; only works with specific architecture; limited to domains with such models available
Statistical issues: small sample sizes, no formal significance testing, relies primarily on SigLIP scores which may not adequately capture geometric plausibility
Missing guidance: paper doesn't explain when method succeeds vs. fails or provide principled approach to predict problematic prompts
Reproducibility concerns: builds on TRELLIS which may not be accessible; no code/data release mentioned; hyperparameter choices lack justification

strengths: Novel and well-characterized problem identification: The 'sink trap' phenomenon is a genuine failure mode in text-to-3D systems that hasn't been systematically studied before, with clear characterization through language diversity metrics and empirical analysis.

Comprehensive experimental validation: Extensive experiments across multiple datasets (DT4D, TRELLIS, FLUX, Stable Diffusion, COCO) with both quantitative metrics (L1, LPIPS, SigLIP) and qualitative results, demonstrating consistent effectiveness.

Practical and effective solution: The unconditional inversion approach is simple, works in practice, and enables high-fidelity semantic 3D editing without auxiliary models—a meaningful improvement over existing pipelines.

Clear presentation and analysis: Well-written paper with effective figures (especially Fig. 1-3) that clearly convey the problem, analysis methodology, and solution. The quantitative analysis of language diversity vs. geometric expressivity is insightful.

Strong empirical insights: Demonstrates that 3D generative models possess substantial geometric expressivity in latent space that is inaccessible through text conditioning, providing valuable understanding of model behavior.
Good reproducibility: Detailed implementation descriptions (Algorithm 1), dataset preparation documentation, and supplementary material enable reproduction of results.
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: The core contribution—using unconditional embeddings during inversion—is a straightforward application of existing null-text inversion techniques (Mokady et al. 2023) to 3D. No novel algorithmic or architectural components.

Lack of theoretical foundation: While the sink trap is characterized empirically, deeper theoretical analysis is absent. No formal explanation of why this mismatch occurs, under what conditions it happens, or guarantees about solution effectiveness. The connection between language diversity and geometric expressivity remains largely empirical.

Incomplete failure mode analysis: Limitations mentioned in Section 6 (instability with simple prompts, extreme cases) are not systematically studied. No clear characterization of OOD-ness, failure frequency, or conditions under which unconditional inversion itself fails.

Limited scope and generalization: Experiments focus almost exclusively on TRELLIS; generalization to other 3D generative models is not explored. Limited comparison with other recent text-guided 3D editing methods—only VoxHammer shown in detail.

Modest quantitative improvements: Table 3 shows non-dramatic improvements (SigLIP: 0.1469 vs 0.0797), raising questions about metric limitations and whether visual improvements fully translate to quantitative gains. Lacks user studies validating editing quality.

Missing critical ablations and analysis: No ablation studies on design choices (CFG scales, why empty vs. other unconditional representations). No computational cost comparison, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, or investigation of why TRELLIS exhibits this phenomenon versus other models.

Evaluation methodology limitations: Heavy reliance on visual inspection; SigLIP metric only measures text-image alignment, not geometric quality; L1 and LPIPS have known limitations for 3D content. No user studies for editing quality validation.

Incomplete characterization of OOD-ness: The paper doesn't rigorously define what makes a shape OOD versus simply outside the training distribution, limiting understanding of when the method should be applied.

strengths: Novel problem identification: The 'sink trap' phenomenon—where text prompts fail for out-of-distribution shapes due to misalignment between geometric expressivity and linguistic sensitivity—is a genuine and important limitation that advances understanding of text-to-3D models.

Well-grounded empirical analysis: The diversity analysis (Table 1) systematically demonstrates the phenomenon across multiple models (TRELLIS, LN3DiffL, GaussianAnything), showing this is a general issue rather than artifact.
Sound technical approach: The combination of Euler inversion with null-text optimization is theoretically motivated, clearly described, and algorithmically detailed (Algorithm 1).

Comprehensive experimental validation: Multiple evaluation metrics (L1, SigLIP, LPIPS, VLM-based scoring), tests on 3D shapes and 2D images, view-consistent editing results, and reasonable baseline comparisons demonstrate thoroughness.
High-quality practical results: Demonstrates high-fidelity semantic edits on complex non-rigid shapes (Figs. 6, 11-12) with view-consistent rendering, showing meaningful applicability.
Clear presentation and strong visualizations: Effectively communicates the problem (Figs. 1-2) and methodology (Figs. 3-5) with well-written prose.
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: The core contribution—using unconditional priors via null-text inversion—directly applies established 2D image editing techniques (Null-Text Inversion) to 3D. The methodological innovation is incremental rather than fundamental.

Insufficient theoretical understanding: The sink trap is characterized empirically but lacks theoretical explanation for why this misalignment occurs. No principled criteria for predicting when unconditional inversion is necessary versus when text conditioning suffices.

Narrow evaluation scope: Almost all 3D experiments focus on humanoid/animal characters from DT4D dataset. No evaluation on furniture, buildings, vehicles, or other major shape categories. TRELLIS-generated shapes are synthetic and may not represent realistic OOD scenarios.

Unclear applicability characterization: No clear guidance on when unconditional inversion outperforms text-conditioned approaches. High variance in quantitative metrics (Table 3: ±0.008) makes significance assessment difficult. Fig. 9 shows failures but doesn't systematically characterize failure modes.

Incomplete experimental analysis: Missing ablations on key hyperparameters (CFG scale, optimization steps, learning rate). No computational cost or runtime comparisons. No statistical significance testing despite high measurement variance.
Weak baseline comparisons: VoxHammer fails on ~87% of DT4D samples, making it a poor baseline. Limited comparison to other recent 3D editing methods or non-text-based alternatives.

Insufficient characterization of bounds: Section 6 acknowledges fundamental limitations but provides no quantitative characterization or practical guidance on how far shapes can deviate from training distribution before method fails.

Design choices lack justification: Algorithm 1 shows 10 inner optimization steps and Adam optimizer without ablations or justification. The diversity metric R = Δvis/Δtext is informal and post-hoc without principled motivation.

Comprehensive experimental setup with multiple metrics (L1, LPIPS, velocity norms, VLM evaluation) across multiple datasets
Detailed supplementary material with implementation details and dataset specifications

Narrow evaluation scope: only TRELLIS model tested; 'OOD' validation primarily uses in-distribution variants (TRELLIS-generated, DT4D shapes); no systematic OOD benchmark

Artificial experimental design using approximate prompts rather than genuine user edits; no ablation studies on critical hyperparameters (CFG scale, optimization iterations)
Limited baseline comparisons; only compares against VoxHammer and TRELLIS native editing without recent 3D editing methods; no user studies
Missing analysis: no systematic failure mode investigation, no computational efficiency measurements despite efficiency claims, no sensitivity analysis on OOD-ness gradient
Unsupported core claims such as 'models possess ability to produce vast diversity of shapes' and 'first systematic investigation' given limited scope
Reproducibility concerns: code availability not mentioned, no clear dataset accessibility, some details relegated to appendix

strengths: Clearly identifies and rigorously analyzes the 'sink trap' phenomenon—a fundamental limitation of text-conditioned 3D generative models when dealing with out-of-distribution prompts, with both qualitative and quantitative evidence (language diversity metrics, velocity norm analysis)
Proposes an elegant and practical solution using unconditional (empty prompt) embeddings that requires no architectural changes and is immediately applicable to existing models

Provides comprehensive experimental validation across multiple metrics (L1, LPIPS, SigLIP, CLIP) with comparisons to multiple baselines, demonstrating geometric consistency and high-quality visual results
Makes an important distinction between failures due to text-reasoning capability mismatch versus geometric inexpressivity, with clear evidence and implications
Well-presented with effective visualizations, clear algorithm descriptions, and extensive supplementary material including detailed implementation details
weaknesses: Limited generalization beyond TRELLIS: While claiming to analyze 3D generative models broadly, validation is almost exclusively on TRELLIS. Only passing mentions of attempts on other models with no results presented, limiting claims about the sink trap being a general phenomenon
Moderate technical novelty: The core contribution—using empty prompts during inversion—is somewhat incremental and lacks algorithmic innovation beyond the empirical observation itself

Incomplete theoretical understanding: While empirically showing that empty prompts stabilize trajectories, the paper lacks deep theoretical explanation of why this works or detailed analysis of latent space structure leading to OOD drift
Limited guidance on when to use unconditional versus conditional embeddings, and no clear indicators for detecting when shapes fall outside the recovery range of the method

Geometric expressivity evaluation uses only 13 DT4D character sequences, which seems limited for drawing general conclusions; L1 voxel-space reconstruction may not align optimally with perceptual quality metrics

Method fundamentally bounded by the generative model's learned distribution with no mechanism to handle shapes far outside this distribution; acknowledgment of limitations in extreme OOD cases but no detailed analysis
Reproducibility concerns: Code availability not mentioned; some hyperparameter choices (e.g., CFG scale of 5) under-justified; edit prompts not consistently detailed throughout the main paper
